code: sample.types <- unique(as.character(data.se$sample.type)) sample.types <- sample.types[!is.na(sample.types) & nzchar(sample.types)] |>   setdiff(c("Blank", "QC"))  for (stype in sample.types) {   out.dir <- file.path(proj.dir, "Statistic", stype)   dir.create(out.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)   fig.pdf <- file.path(out.dir, "Figures.pdf")   diff.xlsx <- file.path(out.dir, "diff.metabolites.xlsx")    data.se1 <- data.se[, data.se$sample.type == stype]   data.se.p <- DEP_preprocess(data.se1)    # volcano without p-adjustment   data.diff <- DEP_test_diff(data.se.p, type = "all")   data.diff <- DEP_add_rejections(data.diff, p.adjust = FALSE)   p.diff <- ggplot_sum_patchwork(DEP_plot_volcano(data.diff, "all"))   export_graph2pdf(p.diff, fig.pdf, width = 10, height = 10)    # volcano with p-adjustment + export table   data.diff <- DEP_test_diff(data.se.p)   data.diff <- DEP_add_rejections(data.diff, p.adjust = TRUE)   p.diff <- ggplot_sum_patchwork(DEP_plot_volcano(data.diff, "all"))   export_graph2pdf(p.diff, fig.pdf, width = 10, height = 10, append = TRUE)   table.diff <- DEP_get_diff_table(data.diff, contrast = "all", keep.all = TRUE)   xlsx.write.list(table.diff, diff.xlsx)    # significant features heatmap   data.diff <- DEP_test_diff(data.se.p, type = "all")   data.diff <- DEP_add_rejections(data.diff, p.adjust = FALSE)   data.hm <- DEP_filter_significant(data.diff)   hm <- DEP_plot_heatmap(data.hm)   export_graph2pdf(hm, fig.pdf, width = 10, height = 20, append = TRUE) }

what: Important: z does not convert m/z → formula mass
title: Rdisop mass decomposition (`decomposeMass`)
text: Rdisop’s z full ESI charge-state converter. Empirical check (mass = 203.0526, CHNO, 5 ppm): Correct pre-conversion calling decomposeMass (bare charge / electron correction; adducts still separate): Msearch=m/z×|z|±z⋅M_{\text{search}} = m/z \times |z| \;\pm\; z \cdot m_e m/z = 203.0526, z = 2 must decompose ~406.1 Da, 203 101.5. 101.5 getMolecule(..., z = 2) reports ~203 Da formula (output m/z). 406 mass scale 2+ ion whose observed m/z 203. MassTools::calcMF mz + z * m_e calls decomposeMass — also multiply |z|, gap |z|>1|z| > 1. Rule formula calculator: convert m/z → search mass (mz * |z| ± z*/adduct correction via MSCC), call decomposeMass(..., z = 0) (z = ±1 intentionally want ion-parity semantics already-converted mass). MSdev / MSCC split:
code: getFormula(decomposeMass(203.0526, ppm = 5, z = 1, elements = elements)) # C4H7N6O4, C3H11N2O8, ... getFormula(decomposeMass(203.0526, ppm = 5, z = 2, elements = elements)) # same list — still ~203 Da formulas, not ~406 Da getMass(getMolecule("C4H7N6O4", z = 2)) # ~101.5259  ← display m/z only, not what decomposeMass searches

title: Rdisop mass decomposition (`decomposeMass`)
text: decomposeMass thin wrapper: Core problem (Money Changing Problem / MCP): Find non-negative integers (nC,nH,nN,…)(n_C, n_H, n_N, \ldots) ∑ne⋅\sum n_e \cdot m_e lies within mass tolerance window. Typical R call: Useful accessors: getFormula(), getMass(), getScore(), getValid(), getIsotope(). measured isotope peaks, prefer decomposeIsotopes(masses, intensities, ...) — enumeration core, better ranking.
code: decomposeMass(mass, ppm, ...)   → decomposeIsotopes(c(mass), intensity = 1, ...)   → C++ Money-Changing / mass-decomposition solver library(Rdisop)  elements <- initializeElements(c("C", "H", "N", "O")) results <- decomposeMass(   mass = 203.0526,   ppm = 5,   z = 1,   elements = elements ) getFormula(results)

title: Rdisop mass decomposition (`decomposeMass`)
code: target mass + ppm (+ mzabs)         │         ▼ build element alphabet (monoisotopic masses), sorted by mass         │         ▼ MCP / mass decomposition   → all integer vectors n with |Σ n·m − mass| ≤ tol         │         ▼ optional chemical validity (DBE, nitrogen rule, …)         │         ▼ molecule objects (formula, exactmass, score, isotopes, …)

title: Rdisop mass decomposition (`decomposeMass`)
text: Naive enumeration (nested loops atom counts) scales roughly ∏e(nemax+1)\prod_e (n_e^{\max}+1) — exponential number element types bounds grow mass. Rdisop / DECOMP . uses efficient MCP algorithms (dynamic programming + smart backtracking; Böcker & Lipták): Finds compositions whose mass falls tolerance window Runtime typically closer proportional number solutions, full nested-loop lattice walk Far better memory profile classical full DP tables problem : yes, enumerates mass-matching compositions allowed elements; , dumb “try every combination” search.

what: 3.4 Missing pairs: why xcms avoids the fill problem (and MSdev does not)
title: Feature grouping with `EicSimilarityParam`
text: xcms EicSimilarityParam MSdev_group_feature_EIC end similarity-matrix clustering, build different similarity inputs. xcms (many small dense matrices) RT (optional abundance) grouping first → hierarchical FG.xxx… EIC similarity runs inside existing feature_group Within subset, every pair scored (compareChromatograms) dense nft × nft matrix initialized NA_real_ Labels refined FG.xxx → FG.xxx.yyy Cross-RT features never share matrix, xcms decide fill “uncompared” global pairs. Failed correlations inside group stay NA (0). MSdev custom path (one global matrix) Candidate edges: |rtmed_i − rtmed_j| < rt_tol (sparse) Densify one full matrix clustering Pairs outside rt_tol absent must filled fill controlled absent_sim xcms_group_feature_EIC / MSdev_group_feature_EIC: Related bug: large densified matrix NA absents, MsFeatures::groupSimilarityMatrix can assign wrong group ID joining existing group (integer positional indexing vs named group IDs). MSdev therefore uses groupSimilarityMatrix_completeLinkage() (complete-linkage rule, fixed named-key lookup) inside xcms_group_feature_EIC.
code: xcms:   many small matrices  → no global absent-fill problem MSdev:  one total matrix     → absent_sim (0 vs NA) matters

Pairwise EIC similarity per sample selected sample, compare chromatograms MSnbase::compareChromatograms(): align retention times (ALIGNFUN = alignRt, default closest scan matching) score similarity (FUN = cor → Pearson correlation default) See §4.2 closest vs approx, matched RT subset enters score. Aggregate across samples feature pair, sample-wise scores aggregated 75% quantile. title: Feature grouping with `EicSimilarityParam`
text: alignRt(x, y, …) returns chromatogram : length y retention times y comparison grid always y’s RT vector. Intensities x mapped onto grid; unmatched positions become NA. cor(..., use = "pairwise.complete.obs") keeps positions intensities finite. Consequence: unequal EICs (e.g. 5 vs 20 points) force full 20-point comparison. matched RT subset contributes correlation. onlyPeak = TRUE, intensities outside chrom peaks removed first, many EICs become sparse/short matched subset can small.
code: c1: 5 points   ──align onto──►  c2's 20 RT grid c2: 20 points  ──────────────►  length-20 intensities  Matched RTs (non-NA on both sides) → often ≤ 5 points Unmatched RTs of c2               → NA on aligned c1 → dropped by pairwise.complete.obs

title: Feature grouping with `EicSimilarityParam`
text: closest + tolerance = 0 (current default): Keep match RTs exactly equal. two features extracted different peak windows slightly different scan sets, overlap can shrink handful shared scans. Correlation 3–5 shared points can look high even longer EIC’s shoulders ignored. approx: Maps x onto every RT y via stats::approx (linear). Better want “shape common RT axis” rather “exact shared scans”. Still magic: x’s RT range small subset y, RT interval gets meaningful interpolated values; outside stays NA dropped pairwise.complete.obs.
code: closest, tolerance = 0   x RTs:  •  •  •           (3 scans)   y RTs:  •••••••••••••••••• (many scans)   keep:   only exact RT hits → small subset  approx   x RTs:  •  •  •   y RTs:  ••••••••••••••••••   fill:   interpolate x onto y RTs inside x's RT span   keep:   denser series (still NA outside x's RT range)

what: 6. How MSdev wraps the stock path
title: Feature grouping with `EicSimilarityParam`
text: MSdev::xcms_get_feature_group() runs three xcms/MsFeatures stages order (stage can skipped NULL). See also §3.1. Internal sequence: Reset featureGroups <- NA RT: MsFeatures::SimilarRtimeParam(diffRt, groupFun = groupHclust) Abundance: MsFeatures::AbundanceSimilarityParam(threshold = intCor, transform = log2), filled = TRUE EIC: xcms::EicSimilarityParam(threshold = eicCor, n = 2) SerialParam() (EIC step heavy; serial avoids parallel /O issues) Result: xcms object updated feature_group column; inspect xcms::featureGroups() / featureDefinitions(). skip EIC (e.g. quick draft grouping):
code: xcms_get_feature_group(   xcms.xcms,   diffRt = 5,     # SimilarRtimeParam window (seconds)   intCor = 0.5,   # AbundanceSimilarityParam threshold   eicCor = 0.5    # EicSimilarityParam threshold; n fixed to 2 ) xcms_get_feature_group(xcms.xcms, eicCor = NULL)

title: Feature grouping with `EicSimilarityParam`
text: Cost: EIC grouping loads chromatograms raw files. Pre-group tightly; keep n small. raw data → EIC step: object must still point accessible spectra files. Gap filling vs EIC: abundance step MSdev uses filled = TRUE; EIC step uses peak-restricted chromatograms default (onlyPeak = TRUE), different signal definition. EIC ≠ exact per-sample peak ranges: get_xcms_feature_chromatogram() (like xcms) uses one m/z–RT box per feature; shapes approximate, identical sample’s chromPeak window. compareChromatograms RT subset: default closest + tolerance = 0, exact shared RTs contribute cor (often much fewer points longer EIC). See §4.2 (closest vs approx). start features huge n: sample selection becomes biased runtime explodes. Hierarchical IDs: later steps split within existing groups; re-merge across RT-distant groups.

title: Fast chromatogram extraction (xcms vs MSdev triad)
text: chromatogram(object, mz, rt) Input: user-supplied mz / rt matrices (one box per row). Output: regions × samples chromatograms. featureChromatograms(object, features, …) Needs correspondence (featureDefinitions). One shared mz–RT box per feature (default: min/max feature’s peaks via featureArea). box applied every selected sample → rows = features, columns = samples. Important: EIC sample exactly sample’s peak; feature-global box. attaches feature-linked chromPeaks (needed later removeIntensity(..., "outside_chromPeak")). chromPeakChromatograms(object, peaks, …) Needs peak picking . peak uses mzmin/mzmax/rtmin/rtmax, extracted owning sample. Layout: peaks × 1 column (exact peak shape).

title: Fast chromatogram extraction (xcms vs MSdev triad)
text: Per sample (inside .chromatograms_for_peaks): Cost ≈ N_boxes × N_scans × cost(mz_filter) interpreted R, plus S4 construction per cell. featureChromatograms adds second nested loop features × samples slot chromPeaks cell. Sample parallelism (chunkSize / BPPARAM) helps across files. fix per-file feature-outer kernel. default chunkSize = 2, many workers sit idle.
code: for each box i:                              # feature-outer   keep <- scans whose RT is in box i         # ~all scans if full RT   for each kept scan:     intensity <- max/sum(peaks in mz window)   → build Chromatogram S4 object flowchart TD   boxes["N mz-rt boxes"]   chunk["Chunk samples chunkSize default 2"]   load["Load peaksData for chunk"]   kernel[".chromatograms_for_peaks"]   featLoop["for each box"]   scanLoop["for each scan in RT window: mz filter + aggregate"]   s4["Chromatogram S4 per cell"]   attach["feature path: Nf x Ns peak attach"]   boxes --> chunk --> load --> kernel   kernel --> featLoop --> scanLoop --> s4 --> attach
